candidates.title: Adversarial fashion defeats store AI surveillance
candidates.shift: Wearable 'digital camouflage' clothing designed to defeat AI video-detection systems is emerging as a public countermeasure to computer-vision surveillance.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if such countermeasures spread, retailers relying on CV for loss-prevention, occupancy or queue analytics face an escalating cat-and-mouse dynamic; also a privacy-politics flashpoint.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen reports designer Simon Weckert's 'Digital Camouflage' shirt stops AI video detection, made in response to a Berlin transit AI-surveillance pilot.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of adversarial design against ubiquitous computer vision, driven by privacy pushback against public/retail surveillance. If it scales, CV-based loss-prevention and analytics systems would need redundant sensing modalities.
candidates.author: Starr Charles

candidates.title: Emerging risk category: social robots as crime instruments/victims
candidates.shift: Scholarship is mapping a nascent domain where deployed social robots become instruments or targets of crime (harassment, hacking, vandalism) with no settled liability framework.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: as service/security robots enter stores and public spaces, operators and insurers may need wholly new liability and incident-response categories that don't exist yet.
candidates.evidence: Crime Science scoping literature review on social robots and future crime across education, policing, healthcare and entertainment contexts.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from robots-as-tools to robots-as-legal/criminological subjects, driven by proliferation of social robots in public-facing roles. If it matures, retailers deploying service or security robots would need new insurance products and incident protocols.
candidates.author: Sarah Y Zheng, Shane D. Johnson, Paul Ekblom et al.

candidates.title: Confined-space robot navigation matures for storage infrastructure
candidates.shift: LiDAR-based path-planning now solves navigation in tight, dynamic storage geometries (silos), a capability transferable to legacy warehouse and backroom layouts.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: incremental robotics capability that could extend automation into irregular, already-owned storage spaces rather than requiring purpose-built distribution centers.
candidates.evidence: Scientific Reports paper on enhanced D*lite LiDAR navigation system for spiral-driven grain silo robots in confined, dynamic-obstacle spaces.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of robotics moving from open-floor warehouses into confined, irregular legacy storage geometries. If generalized, retailers could retrofit robots into non-standard backrooms rather than rebuilding automated DCs.
candidates.author: Haoran Ma, Fengmin Guo, Yue Li et al.

candidates.title: Construction-in-progress aesthetic becomes permanent workplace design
candidates.shift: A completed workplace project deliberately preserves visible construction traces and exposed structure as a permanent design language rather than finishing over them.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative reframing: could signal retailers/landlords adopting 'unfinished'/raw construction aesthetics to cut fit-out cost and time, blurring the line between construction phase and occupancy.
candidates.evidence: ArchDaily feature on 'Semi-construction Site Office' by ARCHWASTE in Shanghai, keeping construction traces and exposed structure visible in daily use.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from construction-as-temporary-disruption to construction-aesthetic-as-finished-product, driven by cost/speed pressure and industrial-chic taste. If it spreads, retail fit-outs could skip finishing trades, compressing store-opening timelines and budgets.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Modular timber construction scaling into irregular sites
candidates.shift: Prefabricated modular timber systems are now flexible enough for irregular, sloped, or forested sites rather than only standardized volumes.
candidates.ai_read: Trend-adjacent: modular construction is well established, but here it demonstrates handling site-specific irregularity, suggesting a maturity that could extend to compact infill retail sites.
candidates.evidence: Dezeen feature on Papundekl Architects' modular timber home with sloped glazed facade on a South Bohemian forest site.
candidates.initial_analysis: Incremental extension of the modular-construction trend to non-standard, constrained sites. If generalized, it could let retailers build small-format stores faster on awkward urban infill parcels.
candidates.author: Starr Charles

candidates.title: Absence: no established value-chain logic for reused structural components
candidates.shift: Research into Design-for-Disassembly finds that circular reuse of structural building components lacks established business models and regulatory support despite being technically feasible.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative absence signal: construction and finance need new contract types, warranties, and building codes for reused structural elements before circular building can scale.
candidates.evidence: Circular Economy and Sustainability paper on business/value-chain logics for reusable structural components, citing regulatory adoption as the barrier.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from linear demolition/build-new construction to a component-reuse economy, driven by decarbonization pressure. If realized, retail landlords could source certified reused structural steel/columns, requiring warranty and code categories that don't yet exist.
candidates.author: Jaakko Annala, Tuomo Joensuu, Lauri Alkki et al.

candidates.title: Absence: standardized material-stock accounting for embodied carbon
candidates.shift: New ML-driven dynamic material stock-and-flow models aim to quantify embodied emissions across the built environment, filling a missing measurement infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could become the accounting backbone future zoning/finance rules need to price embodied carbon in real estate — a category that is largely absent today.
candidates.evidence: Study responding to the building/construction sector's ~37% share of global emissions, developing an ML plus dynamic material-stock-and-flow framework.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from unmeasured to model-based tracking of embodied carbon in building material stocks. If adopted by regulators/insurers, retail real-estate portfolios could face embodied-carbon disclosure requirements akin to today's operational-energy reporting.
candidates.author: Qiyu Liu

candidates.title: Durability-adjusted circular concrete gains a cost/LCA framework
candidates.shift: A new life-cycle assessment method integrates durability and end-of-life circularity for recycled-aggregate concrete, moving it from niche toward a comparably-specified material.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if durability parity is proven at scale, recycled concrete could enter mainstream procurement specs, lowering the barrier to circular construction in retail builds.
candidates.evidence: Discover Concrete and Cement study on hybrid-treated recycled aggregate concrete cradle-to-cradle LCA/LCC in Germany.
candidates.initial_analysis: Incremental move toward provable durability-circularity tradeoffs in concrete, driven by carbon-reduction mandates. If it matures, recycled aggregate could become a default specification in store construction contracts.
candidates.author: Sandeep Singh, Bashar Tarawneh, Bhargav P. Majmundar et al.

candidates.title: Absence: gender-specific occupational heat-safety standards
candidates.shift: A systematic review finds occupational heat-exposure standards don't adequately account for sex/gender-related vulnerability differences among workers.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: frontline retail, warehouse and curbside-pickup workers may need differentiated heat-safety protocols and scheduling as climate warms — a standard that largely doesn't exist yet.
candidates.evidence: Research Square systematic review on occupational heat exposure and sex/gender-related vulnerability among women workers.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from generic to demographic-differentiated occupational heat standards, driven by rising heat exposure and workforce composition. If adopted, retailers would need to redesign shift scheduling, PPE, and facility cooling by gender-specific risk.
candidates.author: Wilman Yesid Ardila‐Barbosa, Hermes Ramón Gonzalez Acevedo

candidates.title: Housing-level heat exposure linked to reproductive health disparities
candidates.shift: A study moves from neighborhood-average heat metrics to individual/housing-level exposure, finding disparities in preterm births tied to housing conditions, not just location.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative cross-branch convergence (sustainability x demographic x housing): could push future building codes/insurance toward requiring in-unit cooling standards, not just neighborhood heat-island mitigation.
candidates.evidence: Environmental Research Health study on heat exposure disparities and preterm births by housing type in LA County, using 2015-2022 data.
candidates.initial_analysis: Shift from macro (neighborhood) to micro (housing-unit) heat-exposure accountability, driven by warming climate and health-equity research. If it matures, codes/insurance could require unit-level cooling/heat-resilience tied to health outcomes rather than outdoor heat-island scores alone.
candidates.author: Hasibe Caballero-Gómez, Qi Meng, Jennifer Brady et al.

candidates.title: Cyberattack disrupts physical ordering/shipping at scale
candidates.shift: A cyberattack on a major manufacturer directly halted physical ordering and shipping operations, confirming supply-chain physical flows as a direct cyber-risk surface.
candidates.ai_read: Trend, already covered — included for calibration; the recurring underlying pattern (cyber-physical supply disruption) is relevant to retail DC/fulfillment risk and insurance design.
candidates.evidence: Supply Chain Dive reports Boston Scientific's global ordering and shipping disrupted by a cyberattack.
candidates.initial_analysis: Example of a cascading digital-to-physical failure in supply chains, driven by rising cyberattack frequency on manufacturing/logistics IT. If it continues, retailers/insurers will need cyber-resilience requirements built into fulfillment-center design and vendor contracts.
candidates.author: Ricky Zipp

candidates.title: Continued mega-scale automated fulfillment center investment
candidates.shift: A named, already-forecast billion-dollar automated fulfillment center continues the pattern of capital rotating into automated distribution infrastructure.
candidates.ai_read: Trend, already named and widely covered — included for calibration; underlying signal is continued capital concentration into automated fulfillment real estate versus store-based fulfillment.
candidates.evidence: Supply Chain Dive: Walmart to build a 1.5M sq ft, $1.3B automated fulfillment center in Georgia, breaking ground this year.
candidates.initial_analysis: Continuation of the shift from store-based to dark-fulfillment-center-based retail logistics, driven by automation ROI and e-commerce growth. If it continues at this pace, real-estate capital keeps rotating away from storefront square footage toward automated distribution nodes.
candidates.author: Kelly Stroh
